findings.evidence: Output names the skill's review table and then overrides it ('one table per screen instead of one', 'a ` — priority:` suffix inside evidence cells', 'prose around the tables') without showing the resulting header or one filled row.
findings.fix: Under Output, add one filled example row in the overridden form (rule | pass/fail/na | evidence with the priority suffix | fix) so the table shape is visible without reconstructing it from the skill.

findings.evidence: Gotchas by input covers code and URL or mockup, but not a screenshot: step 2's checklist says screenshots hide touch-target scale, hover, focus, error and loading, and that limit is never a gotcha.
findings.fix: Add a screenshot bullet: a still hides touch-target scale, hover, focus, error and loading, so those stay unverified until code or a render supplies them.

findings.evidence: Research checks ends on a menu of five trend issues (glassmorphism, neumorphism, parallax, tiny body text, text over busy images) with no default for which to check first.
findings.fix: Name a default order: contrast and legibility (text over busy images, glassmorphism, neumorphism, tiny body text) before motion (parallax), since a contrast failure is already an accessibility blocker.

findings.evidence: Output step 2 says a decision with no screen skips the review table and sets 'biggest win = the recommended alternative, or the step-3 hypothesis and the test that settles it', while step 4 always requires 'Biggest win, or an explicit outcome (below)' and the next paragraph says that outcome replaces the biggest win when an applicable criterion is unverified. A decision whose evidence cannot separate the alternatives and whose test cannot be run has a recommended alternative (step 3) and an untested hypothesis, so both clauses apply and the section never says which one step 4 prints.
findings.fix: State the order: when step 3 both recommends the highest-ranked alternative and leaves a hypothesis untested, step 4 prints the recommended alternative as the biggest win and names the untested hypothesis beside it; the observation-or-test outcome replaces the biggest win only when a screen criterion is unverified and no failure is proven.
